=={{header|Cxc}}==

Cxc has no recursive functions; recursion folds into the atom lifecycle. The two running fields <code>a</code> and <code>b</code> hold <code>(F(i), F(i+1))</code>. Each <code>tick</code> prints <code>a</code>, advances <code>(a, b)</code> to <code>(b, a + b)</code> via the <code>=></code> transition arrow (one-shot field update for the next state), increments <code>i</code>, and self-sends until <code>i == 20</code>.

<syntaxhighlight lang="text">
def main:
    a: Int! = 0
    b: Int! = 1
    i: Int! = 0

    -> running
        then: self :> tick

    running <: tick -> running
        |: i < 20
        then:
            print(a.to_string())
            a => b
            b => a + b
            i => i + 1
            self :> tick

    running <: tick -> end
        |: i == 20
</syntaxhighlight>

The <code>=></code> arrow is distinct from assignment: it declares the new value of a field for the next state. Within a single arm body, reads of <code>a</code>/<code>b</code> see the entry snapshot, so <code>b => a + b</code> uses the pre-tick <code>a</code> even though the preceding line stages a new <code>a</code>. Two arms on <code>tick</code> dispatch by guard; the first whose <code>|:</code> proposition holds fires.
